standard_prerequisites.name: The rational bridge setup
standard_prerequisites.use: Proof lines 6344-6345: k''/k'/k are the field extensions of the example; k'/k is finite separable and [k'' : k'] = 2.

standard_prerequisites.name: Cohomology under flat base change
standard_prerequisites.use: Proof lines 6354-6356: H^1(C_K, O_{C_K}) = 0 by flat base change, so each C_i has genus 0 over K'_i.

core_obligations: The product decomposition (proof lines 6344-6350): since k'/k is finite separable, k' \otimes_k K = K'_1 x ... x K'_n is a finite product of finite separable extensions K'_i/K; the corresponding decomposition k'' \otimes_k K = prod K''_i gives degree 2 separable algebra extensions K''_i/K'_i.
The components (lines 6352-6356): set C_i = C_{K'_i}; then C_K = disjoint union of the C_i, and each C_i has genus 0 as a curve over K'_i because H^1(C_K, O_{C_K}) = 0 by flat base change.
The intersection degree (lines 6358-6359): finally X'_K \cap C_i = Spec(K''_i) has degree 2 over K'_i, so each C_i is a rational bridge in the sense of the example.
proof_roadmap: Decompose the scalar extensions using separability of k'/k.
Split C_K into components and keep genus 0 via flat base change.
Check the degree-2 intersection condition componentwise.
difficulty_reason: Stability lemma (statement 6340-6343, proof 6344-6359): after any base field extension a rational bridge becomes a finite disjoint union of rational bridges - the proof runs through the separable product decomposition of the scalar extensions, the genus-0 property preserved by flat base change, and the componentwise degree-2 intersection; every step is justified and nothing is omitted. H2: separable algebra bookkeeping.
